Real estate tip

Home inspections in the GTA: what to expect

What it costs, what the inspector looks at, what they don't, and how to use the report.

Ali Bayat
Figures checked against the sources below on November 21, 2026
Published November 21, 2026
2-minute readFor buyers and sellersOntario

01Before you book

$350–$600Typical feePer the Government of Ontario; larger homes cost more
Go alongAttend the inspectionOntario recommends it; ask questions as you go
Not licensedIn OntarioInspectors aren't required to be licensed or insured: ask

02What they check

Structure

Foundation and framing

Cracks, movement and signs of water.

Roof and exterior

Shingles, flashing, grading

Age, wear and where water drains.

Plumbing

Supply, drains, water heater

Leaks, pipe materials and water pressure.

Electrical

Panel and wiring

Capacity, safety issues and older wiring types.

Heating and cooling

Furnace, AC

Age, condition and service history.

Interior

Windows, doors, attic

Insulation, ventilation and moisture.

03What an inspection isn't

  • Not pass or failIt's a visual report on condition.
  • Not a code or zoning checkIt won't tell you if a unit is legal.
  • Not behind wallsMould and hidden damage can be missed.
  • Not a warrantyNothing is guaranteed after closing.

04Using the report

  1. 01

    Sort the findings

    Same day

    Safety issues, big-ticket items, and routine maintenance.

  2. 02

    Get quotes for big items

    Within your condition period

    A roofer's or electrician's quote beats a guess.

  3. 03

    Decide

    Before conditions expire

    Proceed, ask for a price reduction or credit, or walk away.

Ali's take

Hire your own inspector and walk the house with them. An hour of questions is worth more than the 40-page report.
